# Disc Image Studio: Drawing Pictures on Optical Discs Using Burned Data

**Source:** https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfcTA74D4Bs/ · **Type:** Reel · **Author:** Git Hype · **Saved:** 2026-11-24

## Summary

Disc Image Studio allows users to burn visual artwork directly onto standard optical media (CDs, DVDs, Blu-rays) without printing. It converts images into dithered binary data, maps them onto the disc's spiral track, counteracts drive-level data scrambling via pre-masking, and compensates for real-world track pitch curvature.

## Transcript and on-screen text

This picture isn't printed on the disc. It's data. Disc Image Studio makes it. Pick a blank CD, DVD, or Blu-ray, and import an image. The Tone panel turns it into black and white dots. A DVD's data runs along one spiral track, about 46,000 turns. The app walks it, asking which pixel lands here? Dark pixel: byte A5. Light pixel: byte 92. Each burns a different texture, so you see dark or light. Burners scramble data, so the app pre-scrambles it to cancel that. Export an ISO and burn it. First burns bend, because real track spacing varies. Burn a test target, trace its photo, and the app fits your disc. Now lines land straight, and your picture appears. Ordinary discs, ordinary burners: over 7,700 stars. The catch: results vary by disc and by burner. Use spare discs. Disc Image Studio. Link on GitHub.
